summary: Discovery call focused on EverGrove's requirements for a private Redwood deployment inside their AWS environment. Key constraints: strict data residency for EU customers, egress inspection via central proxy, no internet egress from model hosts, and need for SSO + KMS integration. Team agreed on pilot scope and next steps.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-08-14
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 7 minutes (recording truncated for notes)
- Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Khanna (EverGrove Head of Cloud), Leah Ortiz (EverGrove Security), Tom Boyle (EverGrove SRE)

Summary: (auto) quick overview of constraints and ask, notes may be imperfect

Topics: private endpoints, peering vs Transit GW, region gating, audit logs, KMS/HSM

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off — can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Samir Khanna: yes loud and clear, thanks Ava
[00:08] Leah Ortiz: yep, good to go
[00:12] Ava Martinez: cool. quick agenda, i want to understand your network topology, egress controls, region restrictions and security checkboxes. ravi will cover architecture options and we can map out next steps.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: hi all, ravi here, i'll try to be brief then we can deep dive. at a high level for Private we typically offer two patterns: peering/transit gateway style to our private control plane, or PrivateLink endpoints in each region, and then the option for an on-prem agent if you need air-gap.
[00:42] Tom Boyle: so the big thing for us is we can't have model hosts talk to public internet. everything must go through our egress inspection stack, which is a central proxy in eu-west-1 — and we do snort/ids there.
[00:55] Leah Ortiz: also we have data residency constraints: EU customers' prompt data must remain in eu regions and logs need to be retained in-country for 90 days and then archived to our on-prem vault.
[01:10] Ravi Patel: got it. two quick clarifying q's: is the eu requirement for all workloads or just a subset? and do you have an existing Transit GW or are you using VPC peering?
[01:22] Samir Khanna: subset — about 35% traffic is EU-only. we have a Transit Gateway in place, yes.
[01:28] Ava Martinez: okay that helps. from a Redwood standpoint we can pin serving to eu-west-1 model replicas and use routing policies to keep EU customer traffic in region. we also support private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) per region so traffic never leaves AWS backbone.
[01:44] Tom Boyle: with PrivateLink do you still need peering? i'm trying to avoid expanding our peering table.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: PrivateLink avoids peering by exposing an interface endpoint in your VPC, so you don't need to add routes for every Redwood subnet. That said, if you already centralize egress via a Transit GW we can attach through that as well. there's some tradeoff: PrivateLink is simpler for security teams, Transit is better for centralized routing and shared services.
[02:10] Leah Ortiz: what about kms? our legal team insists on customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[02:15] Ava Martinez: we support CMK integration with your kms. for Private deployments we can either have a dedicated kms policy or bring-your-own hsm if required, and we capture audit logs for key usage.
[02:28] Samir Khanna: audit logs — is that at token-level or request-level? our compliance folks want lineage on prompts and model outputs to tie back to customer records.
[02:38] Ravi Patel: our audit logs are request-level and include headers, model id, route, timestamp, and we can include user ids if you pass them in the request. token-level costs are in the cost logs in the console but token reconstruction is something we can discuss for the pilot.
[02:54] Leah Ortiz: we need SOC2-type attestations and an assurance of encryption in-flight and at-rest. do you have a SOC2 report?
[03:00] Ava Martinez: yes for the hosted service we have SOC2, and for Private we provide the same baseline documents plus deployment hardening guides. i'll drop the security pack after the call.
[03:12] Tom Boyle: latency — we saw performance degradation from a competitor when they were in a different region. what's the typical p95 you see intra-region for a 2k token generation on your dedicated gpu pools?
[03:24] Ravi Patel: p95 depends on model size and batching, but for a 13B quantized model in dedicated mode we often see p95 around 220–350ms per token for streaming. for your use case if we pin in eu-west and control batching it should meet low latency SLOs; we'll run a bench to confirm.
[03:44] Samir Khanna: bootstrapping question — how do you handle kv cache warmup if we route traffic from multiple regions?
[03:51] Ravi Patel: we keep cache per serving pool. if you plan multi-region routing you can choose sticky routing to keep the same customer shards in eu pools. otherwise there is cold-start impact.
[04:05] Ava Martinez: quick note on cost controls — Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization profiles to reduce token spend. for the pilot we'll provide recommendations.
[04:14] Leah Ortiz: one more security nuance: our auditors require that there be no lateral admin access from Redwood to customer VPCs. how is admin access handled?
[04:22] Ravi Patel: for Private we don't provision admin access to your vpc. Our control plane has limited orchestration access, but you provide the endpoints and we never inject credentials into customer subnets. we can walk through runbooks and rbac for the pilot.
[04:36] Samir Khanna: ok big picture sounds plausible. what's the timeline if we want to run a pilot starting end of august?
[04:43] Ava Martinez: doable — typical pilot is 4–6 weeks. action items would be: you send cidrs and egress flow, we share checklist and region matrix, we schedule benching and a security scoping call.
[04:58] Tom Boyle: about egress — we want all egress from model hosts to be forced to our proxy via route table and explicit nacls. can you confirm Redwood hosts will be able to use that path?
[05:08] Ravi Patel: yes that's standard; we can either place model hosts in your vpc using PrivateLink or peer with your vpc and set routes to the proxy. in both cases you control the route enforcement.
[05:20] Leah Ortiz: what about peering ip overlap — we have a couple legacy cidrs. do you support nat overlay or ip remap?
[05:26] Ravi Patel: we don't do ip remap in the network plane; we typically recommend non-overlapping cidrs. if overlap exists the common pattern is to use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) which avoids route table conflicts.
[05:38] Samir Khanna: is there a supported way to keep model logs inside our s3 and never send them to Redwood's control plane?
[05:45] Ava Martinez: yes you can configure log forwarding to your s3 bucket via private transfer. For audit logs we can route a copy into your s3 while storing minimal metadata in Redwood with encrypted pointers. we'll include exact options in the checklist.
[05:58] Tom Boyle: and how about tenant separation on infra? we need assurances that our data is isolated in dedicated pools.
[06:05] Ravi Patel: with Dedicated you get reserved gpu pools and network isolation. Private gives you a customer-controlled vpc and model hosts inside your environment so separation is enforced by network and iam. We'll include separation diagrams.
[06:20] Leah Ortiz: any known blockers for eu-only data?
[06:23] Ava Martinez: only the usual: ensure you pin routing to EU model pools, don't enable global logging to regions outside EU, and set s3 bucket region policies. we have customers who run EU-only with these controls; it's standard.
[06:36] Samir Khanna: ok good. can you send a short architecture sketch for PrivateLink vs Transit GW option?
[06:41] Ava Martinez: yes we'll send both sketches.
[06:43] ------- short silence/notes -------
[06:47] Ava Martinez: recap: next steps — send checklist, region matrix, schedule bench week of Aug 23, security deep dive with Leah. anyone want to add?
[06:56] Leah Ortiz: please include detailed kms integration steps and expected key rotation patterns.
[07:01] Ravi Patel: i'll include benchmark items and sample model sizes + quantization guidance.
[07:06] Tom Boyle: i'll share the vpc diagrams and cidrs by Wednesday.
[07:10] Ava Martinez: perfect. thanks all. i'll follow up with calendar invites and the deck.
[07:15] Samir Khanna: thanks everyone, bye
[07:17] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., 'Rede wood' or 'Redwood' alternates), filler words, and timestamps are automated. The transcript contains paraphrased technical guidance and should be treated as a summary for next steps rather than verbatim legal record.
